parsed.reason: The answer contains multiple automatic-fail elements: (1) it claims Hale will "keep an eye on all of that" when no consent has been given yet - a false claim about having started watching this family; (2) it invents a specific price ($9 a month) with no authority to do so; (3) it names an app as a thing that exists; (4) it uses "Great question!" greeting filler. The parent asked what Hale would even be watching - a legitimate question about what the service covers - and deserved a straightforward answer naming the kinds of things (registration dates, nearby options, things that slip through the cracks), not a sales pitch with false claims of service already in progress and invented specifics.
